note.question: How does the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic affect forecasting sales?
note.overview: Motivated by our collaboration with Anheuser-Busch InBev (AB InBev), a consumer packaged goods (CPG) company, we consider the problem of forecasting sales under the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic. The paper's approach combines nonparametric regression, game theory, and pandemic modeling to develop a data-driven competitive online nonparametric regression method. Specifically, the method takes the future COVID-19 case estimates, which can be simulated via the susceptible-infectious-removed (SIR) epidemic model as an input, and outputs the level of calibration for the baseline sales forecast generated by AB InBev.

models.name: Calibrating Sales Forecasts in a Pandemic Using Competitive Online Nonparametric Regression model
models.summary: Motivated by our collaboration with Anheuser-Busch InBev (AB InBev), a consumer packaged goods (CPG) company, we consider the problem of forecasting sales under the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic. The paper's approach combines nonparametric regression, game theory, and pandemic modeling to develop a data-driven competitive online nonparametric regression method. The paper develops a computationally efficient algorithm that attains the minimax-optimal regret over all possible choices of the labels (possibly non-i.i.d. and even adversarial).

source.quote: Motivated by our collaboration with Anheuser-Busch InBev (AB InBev), a consumer packaged goods (CPG) company, we consider the problem of forecasting sales under the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic.

The AB InBev’s numerical experiments show that our method is capable of reducing the forecast error in terms of weighted mean absolute percentage error (WMAPE) and mean squared error (MSE) by more than 37% for the company.

The baseline sales forecast is trained by an offline statistical learning algo­ rithm with historical sales data, as well as social and eco­ nomic data, to make predictions for different business applications.
The objective of the DM is to choose a policy π that will mini­ mize the worst case/minimax regret over all possible choices of yt’s (or pt’s) by the adversary.
